newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan army death toll from rebel raid mounts.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan army death toll from rebel raid mounts.

text.p: The Sri Lankan army death toll from Tuesday's Tamil Tiger rebel raid rose to 97 on Wednesday as troops cleared the battle zone, the defence ministry said.
It put the guerrilla death toll at 210, including women fighters, though it said the army had so far found the bodies of only 48 rebels.
The Tigers, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils, say more than 300 soldiers were killed for the loss of some 50 guerrillas.
Independent confirmation of events is not possible as international media have not been allowed into the war zone.

A defence ministry statement said more than 1,000 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels took part in the pre-dawn attack on the army's defences at Thandikulam and Nochchimoddai. This is north of the government-held frontline town of Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) north of Colombo.

The rebels tried to attack the army's field headquarters and artillery gun positions at Thandikulam, the statement said. The attack persisted late into Tuesday, but security forces defending positions held on and drove the rebels back, forcing them to withdraw with their dead and wounded.
The ministry statement said 12 officers, 86 troops, and more than 300 rebels were wounded in the attack.
The casualty figures put out by the defence ministry conflicted with the rebels' account of the attack, issued by their clandestine Voice of Tigers radio.
It said a military ammunition dump and a key bridge near Nochchimoddai were destroyed.
The defence ministry statement said the army lost one battle tank while two more were damaged. A helicopter gunship was also damaged by rebel fire.
Troops, realising they were outnumbered by rebels, had destroyed three artillery guns and ammunition to prevent them from falling into enemy hands, it said.
"The gunners had fought back," a military official said. "There were 25 bodies of soldiers near the guns."
An aid worker in Vavuniya told Reuters that 10 civilians, including a seven-year-old girl, had been killed in the fighting and some 35 wounded and taken to Vavuniya hospital.
Thiagarajah Selvathurai, a resident who witnessed the fighting near Thandikulam, described how he saw an army ammunition dump explode after being hit by shells.
"Suddenly, there was a big bang, smoke and the whole area lit up," he told Reuters in Vavuniya. "There were many explosions. Pieces of shrapnel were falling near us."
"We could also see tracer bullets flying overhead and hear bullets hitting houses and trees," he said.
Aid workers and military officials said several civilians, soldiers and 13 policemen were missing after the attack.

The LTTE are fighting for a homeland for Tamils in mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the 13-year-old war. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
